title: Meet the Vegan Draculas of Australia - Nautilus
gist: The Australian brook lamprey, nicknamed 'Vegan Dracula,' is the only known non-parasitic lamprey in the Southern Hemisphere, and Griffith University researchers are working to confirm its identity after discovering it on Queensland's K'gari island.

insights.claim: Most lampreys develop vampiric, blood-sucking feeding behavior in adulthood, but some species instead fast as adults and live off nutrients gained in childhood.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Establishes the unusual life-history trait that makes the species scientifically notable.
insights.locator: some lampreys don’t become parasitic as adults

insights.claim: The Australian brook lamprey (Mordacia praecox) is the only known non-parasitic lamprey in the Southern Hemisphere, earning the nickname 'Vegan Dracula' for its harmless ring of teeth.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Marks a distinct, rare organism of interest to evolutionary and freshwater biology.
insights.locator: The only known lamprey in the Southern Hemisphere that’s not parasitic

insights.claim: Griffith University aquatic ecologists discovered the Australian brook lamprey while electrofishing creeks on K'gari island, Queensland, in 2022.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Shows targeted field methods can surface long-hidden species in well-populated regions.
insights.locator: found living on K’gari island in Queensland in 2022

insights.claim: Researchers believe the species has occurred naturally in Queensland for a very long time but stayed hidden due to its cryptic nature, per co-lead author David Moffatt.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Suggests undocumented native biodiversity persists undetected even in studied areas.
insights.quote: We expect these animals naturally occur in Queensland, and have been here for an awfully long time, but have remained hidden due to their cryptic nature.
